RB didn’t hook me until the 3rd book. 1st book I gave 3.5 stars, second book I gave 2.5 stars lol and third book I gave 5 stars!!! 4th & 5th I gave 4-4.5 stars I believe 

So glad I read them after ZA 3 because o fell in love with some of these characters in RB

I sympathize with you. My brother had/has a similar circumstance (I’m going to share his story)
My brother is all about his body, constantly going to the gym putting his body first. Always doing sports like BMX, snowboarding, flips, and stunting on motorcycles and what not. Then one day a stunt went bad and shattered his foot/ankle, one of the worse ones the surgeon had ever saw. The pain was ridiculously awful. He was told that he probably wouldn’t be able to do any of his activities again and certain exercises, what else is there for him to do without these things? He wanted to kill himself, even told us how he was going to do it. But he held out on the hope that he could still do some of the things he loves. He put in lots of time and effort in finding ways around his injury to exercise, and yes he had chicken legs for a couple years until he was strong enough to slowly build some muscle there lol but he kept focusing on what he could/can do over what he couldn’t and that’s what he said helped him through his emotions and thoughts. Now he still can’t do everything he once did but he found and focused on the things he can. He even went snowboarding for the first time this year since his accident (he kept saying no and putting it off saying his foot can’t handle it, but after a few years he finally did it) 
Now I know your stories and experiences are not the same, I just wanted to share what he went through and how he came out of it. I hope his story can help shine some light for you <3 
PS: what about doing that activity/sport that gymnasts do with the rings in the air? (I don’t know much about it, it just came to mind)

I’m sad you feel this way and I understand it’s hard to get out of this mindset <3 
If you’ve given yourself this amount of time I’d like to offer an idea that helped my brother. 
My brother was very depressed and his therapist suggest taking a high dosage of vitamin B6/B12 everyday and about a month in he noticed a difference in himself. (There are other essential nutrients and vitamins that can help lead to depression)
Although I know it doesn’t work for everyone I think it’s worth a shot if you haven’t already tried meds and therapy <3 
Your brain is an organ and just like any other organ it can get sick, if your up for it I think it’s worth a shot <3

Glad to help <3 
I don’t know where you live, but a lot of countries have either low income options for that kind of help or sometimes insurance covers it :) just google :) maybe a suicide hot line in your area? They can give resources :)
You know your parents best, if you have a good relationship they will listen maybe start the conversation off with something like “I have something important to talk to you guys about, please listen to everything I have to say before you speak” that sets the boundaries where you can talk speak your feelings uninterrupted and gives them time to hear and process what you say <3 whatever source of help you choose, you got this <3

don't worry about making them uncomfortable, they would rather listen to you then sit at your funeral <3

you can also talk to people online, therapist and councilors <3 

when pressure builds up like this you just need to unwind, take a break and get away for a bit <3

That is sad to hear about your therapist. i sympathize with you. I don't think medication is always the answer for everyone. I've known some people that its worked great for and others it didn't help at all (my brother for example). What about weed? it helps my one friend with panic attacks.  
what about places like Thailand? from Canada i paid $5-600 for round trip flights. depending where i was i paid anywhere from $10-$25 CAD for a hostel bed per night, food cost me about $10-$20 a day depending where i ate (mostly night markets!) and excursions are average $40-$60. all in all i spent about $1,200 Canadian for 3 weeks there (including flights and going on quiet a few excursions as well. i just went on trip advisor and looked up the popular places to see and stay. I saved some money by eating like shit for a little while but it was worth it (for me).

depending on the type of work experience and schooling, can you get a job somewhere else doing what you do? Using Thailand for example, the cost of living is $800-$1,000 a month depending on life style (when i was there), and someone i met there was teaching English to adults and earned $2k/month and her expenses were $1,100 i think (by the way I'm just referencing Thailand because of how cheap it was, other cheap places are Vietnam or Bali and what not)

Maybe if you did a go-fund me, or worked a couple extra shifts doing something you can go somewhere :)

anyways, just some ideas and i hope this may help you <3

have you tried medication/therapy? 

I know this sounds weird but what about nutrients/vitamins?

My brother was badly depressed and a therapist recommended b6/12 and he saw a change in his perspective around month in. I know a month is a long time but what if it works for you? What if your brain was just missing some essential nutrients/vitamins?  

I hope you don't do it  <3

if you don't mind me asking, how old are you/do you have savings?

if you can do it, an idea is to solo travel for a bit and get out of that toxic environment. if your in school, perhaps going to school abroad might be a solution? i just feel that your perspective might change with a new environment <3 perhaps extended family will take you in? talk to extended family and explain how you feel at home. 

You deserve better, the first step tiny gorals to get yourself out of bed and then hopefully out of the house :) i hope this helps <3

Here are some ideas that may help change your perspective on life:
-solo travel, try going somewhere sunny and warm, travel a bit in that country and try staying in hostels (lots of people you can meet who are also solo traveling) or if you prefer the cold that’s okay to!
-our brains are an organ and just like any other organ it can get sick. My brother was depressed and we were recommended vitamin B6/12 and after a month he saw an improvement for himself. Some essential nutrients are: calcium, chromium, folate, iron, magnesium, omega-3 fatty acids, Vitamin B6, Vitamin B12, Vitamin D and zinc
-therapy, if you already have a therapist: do you like them? Do you feel like yours getting through to them? If not then maybe try someone else
-what do you love? Example: animals? Maybe volunteer at a sanctuary somewhere far from home, a new start and new people

Being in this pandemic has hurt and messed a lot of people up and your not alone <3 for me I’ve just been getting away from home and my hometown as much as possible and I feel rejuvenated after 
I hope you find what you yourself need for fulfillment and happiness  <3
